summary.text: Harappa was a settlement in Punjab, Pakistan, near the former course of the Ravi River, and is the type site of the Bronze Age Indus Valley Civilisation.
At its greatest extent in the Mature Harappan phase, the city is believed to have had as many as 23,500 residents living in clay brick houses.
It was the first Indus site excavated by the Archaeological Survey of India, though its significance became clear only after Mohenjo-daro was discovered.

facts.label: Peak population
facts.value: Believed to be as many as 23,500 residents

facts.label: City area
facts.value: About 150 hectares at its greatest extent

facts.label: Railway damage
facts.value: Bricks from the ruins became railway track ballast

facts.label: Prized goods
facts.value: Carnelian and lapis lazuli were among the most valuable trade items

items.prompt: A Harappan toolmaker wants a metal for blades. Which metals were in use at the time?

options.label: Iron and bronze
Copper and bronze
Iron and copper
Iron and steel

items.explain: Although copper and bronze were in use, iron was not yet employed.

items.prompt: Researchers find no sign that Harappan cities were laid waste by invaders. What do they point to instead?

options.label: Natural causes, such as a climate growing drier
A plague carried into the cities by traders
A rebellion against a single powerful king
A sudden flood from the nearby Ravi River

items.explain: There is no sign the cities were laid waste by invaders; the evidence strongly points to natural causes, with the area becoming gradually drier.

items.prompt: Skeletons at Harappa show more injury and infection in the later phases. What does the timing suggest?

options.label: Violence and disease caused the collapse of the cities
Injury rates were highest when the cities were at their height
Invaders brought disease into a thriving city
These signs largely emerged after the decline had begun

items.explain: The increase in trauma and infection appears to coincide with the period of societal decline, suggesting these signs largely emerged after the onset of collapse.

items.prompt: Harappan merchants stamped distinctive seals on goods. What might the seals have been used for?

options.label: Counting the days of a calendar
Paying wages to workers
Identifying property and shipments of goods
Marking the tombs of rulers

items.explain: Distinctive seals were used, among other applications, perhaps for the identification of property and shipment of goods.

items.prompt: Where did Harappan merchants get gold and copper?

options.label: From mines beside the Ravi River
From people in southern India near modern Karnataka
From the Thar Desert
From imports along Egypt's Nile

items.explain: They traded extensively with people living in southern India, near modern-day Karnataka, to procure gold and copper.

items.prompt: Engineers building a railway in the 1850s needed material for the track bed. What happened to the ancient city of Harappa?

options.label: Bricks from its ruins were used for the track
The railway was routed around the ruins to protect them
The ruins were flooded when the Ravi shifted
The ruins were covered by a new amusement park

items.explain: The archaeological site was damaged in 1857 when engineers building the Lahore-Multan railway used bricks from the ruins for track ballast.
